validation_run_id_derivation: PCEVALID- + first 32 uppercase hex of SHA256(researchops-first-live-timing-run-v1 || NUL || raw authorization-ID SHA256 bytes || NUL || execution_environment_id ASCII || NUL || execution_commit ASCII)
rules: Inputs and output caps come unchanged from the two frozen design scenarios; these are not evaluation tasks or tuning data.
One deterministic case handle per frozen scenario makes both scenarios mandatory; at most one attempt per case.
Local-claim origin is explicit and cannot masquerade as an external campaign consumption anchor.
Phase begins after verified local claim and before Key load or fixed-input use; ends after raw/post cleanup and Key-reference release.
The whole-process budget covers preflight/claim and terminalization too; publication cannot measure completion of its own write.
Plan/evidence/publication use distinct first-live schema versions and domains; response-level segment/event linkage and numeric constraints use the shared engine.
Binding contains no fabricated campaign ID, runtime-plan core or external consumption anchor.
Authorization binding and local claim receipt hashes must later be verified against real control artifacts, not trusted from this authoring input.
A timing-complete authoring fixture is not first-live success; actual accepted records must additionally show completed then incomplete_length with the fixed caps.
First-live must actually enable the same collector used by campaign; source presence alone does not satisfy this gate.
A new source profile, runtime authority path, artifact/receipt and review/registry binding must be integrated before this can enable first-live execution.
